description: We’re a team of friends from the Philippines who are into space, tech, and building things that actually get used. We handle coding, design, research, and pitching between us. This year we want to use NASA data to tackle problems that hit close to home, like typhoons, floods, and climate impacts on communities like ours.
summary: Mayon Radar Watch is a free web map that shows where fresh ash, rock and lava may have landed in the river channels around Mayon Volcano, Albay, after its 30 October 2026 eruption. It compares NASA–ISRO NISAR radar images taken 12 days apart. Radar sees through cloud, ash and darkness, so the map works when ordinary satellite photos are blind. Brightness change (GCOV) flags possible new material, and coherence loss (GUNW) raises it to likely. The app ranks the four channels we checked by eye (Basud, Lidong, Mi-isi, Padang), shows a 3D view of the volcano, and makes a printable report for each of 12 nearby towns, reviewed by a person before it is published. Loose material in channels is what heavy rain turns into lahars, so residents and disaster offices need to see it. We locked our rules before the eruption data, tested them on Mayon's July pyroclastic flow and a Panama earthquake, and say plainly that this is not an official warning: follow PHIVOLCS.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mayon Radar Watch maps surface change on Mayon's slopes between two NISAR radar passes on the same track. Users can:

• step through every pass since 21 June 2026 (13 pairs on tracks 104 and 111), including the 14 July pyroclastic flow and the 30 October eruption

• see flagged "new material" as Possible or Likely, in km² and in basketball courts

• rank four checked channels by how much they changed

• search a town for its distance to the crater and whether it is in the Permanent Danger Zone

• open a 3D view on real terrain

• download a formal A4 town report (PDF), with GeoJSON and CSV for QGIS

HOW IT WORKS

A Python pipeline downloads NISAR Level-2 GCOV and GUNW products from the Alaska Satellite Facility, crops them to Mayon and compares two passes. A cell is flagged when its radar brightness changes by more than 3 dB. Coherence loss above 0.3 raises a flagged cell to "Likely" but never adds area. Only land within 10 km of the summit is checked. Results are counted per channel strip (400 m wide) and per town, then published as small files to a static website with no server and no personal data.

HOW WE KEPT IT HONEST

We fixed the thresholds on 1 November, before opening any image taken after the eruption. For the 14 July flow, we compared the gullies PHIVOLCS named (Basud, Bonga and Mi-isi) with the five quiet pairs on the same track. Using brightness alone, each gully flagged more than all five. That check used the provisional threshold and is still a draft. On Panama's 9 October earthquake, the same rule with no tuning matched the University of Panama landslide map (correlation 0.66, against −0.23 for a quiet pair). The first eruption pairs flag 0.79 and 0.88 km² from brightness alone. That is not yet clearly above quiet passes, and we say so. A named reviewer approves every town report. NISAR products are provisional, and the app always says it is not an official warning.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Residents, barangay, MDRRMO and LGU staff get a current, plain-language view of which channels changed, even under cloud. PHIVOLCS, scientists and GIS users get methods, pass IDs and open data. The method is free and reusable at other volcanoes.

CREATIVITY

Instead of making a general deformation map, it asks one local question. Which channels refilled after the eruption, and what does that mean for each town?

TOOLS

Python (asf_search, earthaccess, h5py, rasterio, numpy, scipy, shapely, xarray, matplotlib), Leaflet, MapLibre GL JS, GitHub Pages and Actions, Playwright and axe-core (1,000+ automated tests, including accessibility), Gitleaks, Google Earth Pro.

USE OF AI

Anthropic's Claude helped us understand the challenge and plan the project. Claude Code wrote most of the code, tests and documentation from our plans, and our team made every decision and reviewed the results. Most commits made with Claude are marked "Co-Authored-By: Claude". Town reports come from fixed code templates, not AI. No AI-generated images, audio or data are in the app.

Live site: https://bontojamesrod.github.io/Mayon-Radar-Watch/
